questions.q: What happens if every parameter on a report has a valid default value?
options: The report requires an administrator password to open
The report can no longer be re-run with different parameter values
The report runs automatically the first time it's viewed or previewed, without waiting for reader input
The report ignores all parameters entirely
questions.explain: When all parameters have valid defaults, the report renders immediately on open — the reader can still change values and re-run afterward.

questions.q: What are the three options on the Default Values tab of Report Parameter Properties?
options: No default value, Specify values, Get values from a query
Ascending, Descending, Random
Visible, Hidden, Internal
Text, Integer, Boolean
questions.explain: The Default Values tab offers exactly three choices: no default at all, a literal/expression value you specify, or a value pulled from a dataset query.

questions.q: Which of these is a valid default value expression?
options: A direct reference to a field in the report's main data region
A reference to a control on the report viewer toolbar
=Today()
The report's file name
questions.explain: Globals and common functions like =Today() are valid default expressions. Field names from the report's own dataset cannot be used — defaults are evaluated before that data has run.

questions.q: Why can't a default value expression reference a field from the report's own dataset?
options: Because fields can only be referenced inside text boxes, never parameters
Because Report Builder disables all expressions on the Default Values tab
Because default values are evaluated before the main report dataset has actually run, so there's no field data yet
Because field references are reserved exclusively for filters
questions.explain: Defaults are resolved before the report's data has been retrieved, so there's nothing for a field reference to point to yet — you'd need a separate dataset instead.

questions.q: After a report is published to a Report Server, who can override its design-time default values?
options: An administrator, by setting parameter property values directly on the server
Only the original report author, and only by editing the RDL file
No one — design-time defaults are permanent once published
The report viewer's browser cache automatically overrides them
questions.explain: An administrator can override design-time defaults by setting parameter properties on the report server itself, useful for different defaults across environments without touching the RDL.
